note: SCHEMATIC diagrams, not an anatomical atlas. Outlines are drawn to be recognisable and landmark coordinates are placed by eye against anatomy references; nothing here is measured, registered or to scale. Head sites are ESTIMATED 10-20 positions, not positions measured on anyone's head. `registered_to` is null and stays null.

hand-dorsal-right.label: Right hand, back (dorsal) view
hand-dorsal-right.orientation: Fingers up, thumb on the LEFT. This is the back of your right hand held palm-down in front of you.

FDI belly.note: First dorsal interosseous — the muscle bulge in the web between thumb and index finger. Spread your fingers and it stands up.

FDI belly, distal.note: On the FDI belly, the distal end of a pair laid ALONG the muscle fibres, which run from the web of the thumb toward the base of the index finger.

FDI belly, proximal.note: On the FDI belly, the proximal end of the same pair, back along the fibres toward the wrist. SENIAM's surface-EMG spacing is 20 mm centre to centre, but never more than a quarter of the muscle's length — on a muscle this small that is about 10-15 mm, as close as the electrodes allow without touching.

2nd MCP joint.note: The index-finger knuckle — a bony landmark, which picks up less muscle than soft tissue does.

index fingertip.note: The pad of the index finger, not the nail.

ulnar styloid (wrist).note: The bony bump on the little-finger side of the wrist, where the forearm meets the hand.

marked spot.note: The adhesive dot the attention instruction refers to. Same place as the FDI belly.

torso-front.label: Torso, front view
torso-front.orientation: Facing you — so the subject's RIGHT is on the LEFT of the diagram, as in every clinical figure.

right collarbone.note: Just under the clavicle, subject's right (left of this diagram).

left collarbone.note: Just under the clavicle, subject's left.

left lower ribs.note: Over the lower ribs on the subject's left, below the heart.

right hip.note: Iliac crest — the top of the hip bone, subject's right.

V5 (chest).note: 5th intercostal space, anterior axillary line, subject's left.

limbs-front.label: Limb lead sites
limbs-front.orientation: Facing you — subject's RIGHT is on the LEFT of the diagram.

right ankle.note: Bony inner ankle, subject's right leg.

head-lateral-right.label: Head, right lateral view (subject facing right)
head-lateral-right.orientation: Subject faces RIGHT. Nose and forehead on the right of the diagram, occiput on the left. Mirror this map for the left side of the head — the mirrored map renames itself, because a right mastoid labelled 'left' is exactly the error a placement diagram exists to prevent. Head sites are ESTIMATED 10-20 positions drawn by eye, not measured: find each one on the head with a tape.

Cz (vertex).note: The top of the head: halfway along the nasion-inion line over the vertex, and halfway between the two preauricular points (the small dips just in front of the tragus of each ear). The 10-20 system measures side to side between those points, not between the ear canals. Measure both with a tape — do not eyeball it; a centimetre here is a different place on the scalp.

Oz (occipital).note: Occipital midline, the 10-20 Oz position: 10% of the nasion-inion distance up from the inion, on the midline — roughly 3-4 cm above the bump on an adult head. Measure nasion to inion over the vertex with a tape and mark a tenth of it up from the inion.

Fpz (forehead).note: Mid-forehead, about 10% of the nasion-inion distance above the nasion. Hairless, so the easiest good contact on the head.

nasion.note: The dip at the bridge of the nose, between the eyes. A measuring landmark, not an electrode site.

M2 (right mastoid).note: The bony bump behind and below the right ear. Feel for bone, not the soft tissue in front of it.

A2 (right earlobe).note: The right earlobe. Soft tissue, so it moves with the jaw in a way the mastoid does not.

right ear canal.note: Where the insert earphone sits. Mark the insertion depth on the tube and re-check it every cell — a depth change is a level change, and a level change moves the FFR.

magnet mount (right temporo-parietal).note: Where the magnet or the dummy is taped. MOUNTED BY THE THIRD PARTY, before acquisition begins, and never moved while recording — a magnet moving near the leads induces an artefact perfectly time-locked to the manipulation.

inion.note: The bump at the back of the skull (external occipital protuberance). A measuring landmark for the 10-20 system, not an electrode site: Oz sits 10% of the nasion-inion distance above it.

neck-front.label: Neck and upper chest, front view
neck-front.orientation: Facing the subject. The subject's RIGHT is on the LEFT of this diagram — the usual clinical convention, and the usual place to get it wrong. Every landmark says whose side it is in words.

right SCM belly.note: Over the thickest part of the subject's RIGHT sternocleidomastoid. Ask them to turn their head to the LEFT against your hand — the muscle that stands out is the right SCM.

left SCM belly.note: Over the thickest part of the subject's LEFT sternocleidomastoid. Head turned to the RIGHT against resistance makes it stand out.

right SCM sternal head.note: Low on the subject's RIGHT sternocleidomastoid, where it inserts on the sternum, just up and out from the notch.

left SCM sternal head.note: Low on the subject's LEFT sternocleidomastoid, at its sternal insertion, just up and out from the notch.

sternal notch.note: The hollow at the top of the breastbone, between the collarbones. Easy to find by touch, and bony, so it moves little with breathing.

right mastoid.note: Behind the subject's right ear. Where the right SCM originates; a measuring landmark here, not a site on this map.

left mastoid.note: Behind the subject's left ear. Where the left SCM originates.

stem-vertical.label: Woody stem, side view
stem-vertical.orientation: Stem vertical, ground line at the bottom. The pair goes on ONE side of the trunk with the upper contact above the lower; the third contact is in the soil at the base.

upper stem contact.note: Through the bark into the cambium and outer sapwood, 2-3 mm deep. Not the dead outer bark, which is an insulator and gives a beautifully quiet recording of nothing.

lower stem contact.note: 1 cm below the upper contact, same depth, same side of the trunk. The 1 cm separation is the published electrophytography spacing (Souza et al. 2017; Reissig et al. 2023).

soil at the base.note: In damp soil within a hand's width of the root flare, pushed in far enough to stay wet. A floating third contact is the commonest reason a record is nothing but mains hum.

lower trunk.note: Low on the trunk, near the root flare. An alternative to the soil contact when the earth is too dry to hold one.

opposite side, upper.note: The same height as the upper contact but on the far side of the trunk. A second pair here is what would show whether an excursion propagates.
